text: The Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson fundamentally altered the legal landscape of reproductive rights in the United States. The 6-3 ruling overturned nearly 50 years of precedent established by Roe v. Wade, returning the authority to regulate abortion to individual state legislatures. Since the decision, 14 states have enacted near-total bans, while several others have moved to strengthen legal protections for abortion access. Legal scholars are divided on the long-term implications — some argue the decision respects federalism, while others contend it creates an untenable patchwork of rights that varies by geography.
